DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION NO. 21 s. 2021 9 February 2021 MR. PABLO M. CRESPO SR. Secretary to the Mayor Office of the Mayor Municipality of Patnongin Province of Antique Dear Mr. Crespo: This has reference to your letter dated 19 May 2020 requesting for this Department's legal opinion relative to queries on review by Governors or Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Executive Orders executed by Local Chief Executives of component cities or municipalities. In the letter, it is emphasized that only the Executive Order requires the mandatory review either by the Governor or by the Sanggunian Panlalawigan as provided by Section 30 and 468 of Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160), otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991. Accordingly, the following queries are submitted: Why is it that only the Executive Order requires review by aforesaid authorities? 2. Can the Local Chief Executive enforce the Executive Order even it has not been reviewed by the Governor or by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan ? 3. Is there any legal action that can be imposed to the Local Chief Executive who failed to submit the Executive Order for review by the said reviewing authorities? On query number one, we are of the view that the reason why Sections 30 and 468(1 )(i) of RA 7160 mention only Executive Orders, out of all other issuances that the Local Chief Executive of the component cities or municipalities may issue, for the review of the Governor and/or the Sanggunian, is because the very nature of Executive Orders is of general or permanent character in implementation or execution. We deem it apt to borrow the definition of Executive Orders vis-å-vis that of the Administrative Orders, Memorandum Order, and Memorandum Circular in

Executive Order No. 292 (EO 292), series of 1987 otherwise known as the Administrative Code of 1987. It states in Sections 2, 3, 5, and 6 of Chapter II, Book Ill of EO 292: SECTION 2. Executive Orders.—Acts of the President providing for rules of a general or permanent character in implementation or execution of constitutional or statutory powers shall be promulgated in executive orders. SECTION 3. Administrative Orders.—Acts of the President which relate to particular aspects of governmental operations in pursuance of his duties as administrative head shall be promulgated in administrative orders. SECTION 5. Memorandum Orders.—Acts of the President on matters of administrative detail or of subordinate or temporary interest which only concern a particular officer or office of the Government shall be embodied in memorandum orders. SECTION 6. Memorandum Circulars.—Acts of the President on matters relating to internal administration, which the President desires to bring to the attention of all or some of the departments, agencies, bureaus or offices of the Govemment, for information or compliance, shall be embodied in memorandum circulars. Thus, we can surmise that the reason for such mandatory review is for the provincial government to ensure that the issuances of Executive Orders are within the scope of the authorities, powers, duties, and mandate of the Local Chief Executive considering that these Executive Orders will have general and permanent character in implementation and/or execution. Notwithstanding, we shall endeavor to obtain the legislative wisdom on the matter through the records of the proceedings of the Congressional hearings, meetings, and/or deliberations of the Local Government Code. On second query, we opine in the affirmative provided that the requirements for its effectivity have been complied with. Although in the context of ordinances, we have opined again and again the difference between "effectivity" and "validity." Effectivity is the time by which an ordinance is made effective and can already be implemented and given full force and effect. 1 On the other hand, Validity refers to the substantive I DILG Legal Opinion No. 5, series of 2018, 25 January 2018

requirement of an ordinance whether the same is consistent with the Constitution and laws. We are of the view that this may also be made applicable to Executive Orders. Provided that the procedural requirements for the promulgation of the Executive Order have been complied with, then the same may already be given full force and effect. The validity aspect comes upon the review of the pertinent governor and/or sanggunian panlalawigan whether it is within the scope of the authority of the Office of the Local Chief Executive. On the third query, Section 60 of RA 7160 is relevant. It provides that dereliction of duty is a ground for disciplinary action against an elective local official. It states: SECTION 60. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. — An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office on any of the following grounds: (a) Disloyalty to the Republic of the Philippines; (b) Culpable violation of the Constitution; (c) Dishonesty, oppression, misconduct in office, gross negligence, or dereliction of duty; (d) Commission of any offense involving moral turpitude or an offense punishable by at least prision mayor; (e) Abuse of authority; (f) Unauthorized absence for fifteen (15) consecutive working days, except in the case of members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang bayan, and sangguniang barangay; (g) Application for, or acquisition of, foreign citizenship or residence or the status of an immigrant of another country; and (h) Such other grounds as may be provided in this Code and other laws. An elective local official may be removed from office on the grounds enumerated above by order of the proper court.

Considering that it is the duty of the Local Chief Executive to submit the promulgated Executive Order to the Governor for review, the failure to do so may be cause of disciplinary action against the said Local Chief Executive. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you. Very truly yours, RITY OF THE SECRETARY: INGAN CESO Ill for Local Government OIC-Unders LLLS/LRALLD/42 Copy furnished: DIR. JUAN JOWAN E. INGENIERO Regional Director, DILG-Region VI 6 Pepita Aquino St., Fort San Pedro Iloilo City
